title: Application of artificial intelligence in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Application of artificial intelligence in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · S0001-p1】Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) stands as the sixth most prevalent malignancy globally, with predicted incidence rates expected to rise by approximately 63% by 2050 [1]. Developing from the mucosal epithelial cells of the oral cavity, pharynx, larynx and sinonasal tract, HNSCC is influenced by a wide array of risk factors that vary by anatomical site [2]. High-risk factors include human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, as well as the consumption of alcohol and tobacco [3]. Currently, no screening method has proven effective, and early detection primarily relies on meticulous physical examination. Although certain oral premalignant conditions, including leukoplakia (white patches) and erythroplakia (red patches), may advance to invasive carcinoma, the majority of individuals receive diagnosis at advanced stages without earlier premalignant indicators [4]. Most HNSCC instances manifest as locally advanced conditions, necessitating combined therapeutic approaches. The therapeutic strategy generally encompasses surgical intervention followed by supplementary radiation or chemotherapy plus radiation (termed chemoradiation) based on disease progression [5]. Despite this therapeutic aim towards a cure, a significant number of individuals will face locoregional reoccurrence and/or distant metastasis, leading to unfavourable outcomes [6]. Given the limited therapeutic options, apart from palliative chemotherapy, the need for novel treatments is critical. The rapid advancement of immunotherapy offers promising new opportunities for HNSCC management.

【Introduction · S0001-p3】The rapid advancement of statistical methodologies and big data science has markedly elevated AI’s relevance across various domains of human life [14]. AI aims to simulate human intelligence, thought processes and reasoning models to address problems, facilitate decision-making and automate tasks [15]. Machine learning (ML), a subset of AI, analyzes vast datasets for specific tasks, autonomously constructing predictive models and clusters, which are subsequently analyzed by computational systems [16]. AI is centred on creating ‘thinking machines’ capable of independent decision-making, whereas ML focuses on ‘learning machines’ that execute tasks through data processing and algorithmic frameworks without explicit programming instructions [17]. Deep learning (DL), a subset of ML, utilizes AI-powered algorithms that significantly influence biomedical investigations, individualized medicine and precision healthcare [18]. By examining genomics, pathomics, imaging and additional biological information alongside mathematical models, ML offers new insights into patient profiles [19]. The intersection of medicine and AI has become a rapidly developing field, driving innovation in healthcare applications (Figure 1).

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Application of artificial intelligence in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Introduction · S0001-p2】With an increasingly comprehensive understanding of HNSCC and the rapid advancement of immunotherapy, HNSCC is now recognized as an immunosuppressive disease, and immunotherapy holds substantial promise in reshaping its treatment landscape [7]. Currently, several immune checkpoint blockers that target the programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1)/programmed cell death 1 ligand 1 (PD-L1) pathway have gained regulatory approval across different disease conditions, while additional agents, used alone or in combined approaches, remain under clinical evaluation [6]. In 2016, the PD-1 blocking agents nivolumab and pembrolizumab received authorization for treating recurrent or metastatic HNSCC (R/M HNSCC) in individuals who showed disease progression during or following platinum-based chemotherapy [8]. Subsequently, in 2019, pembrolizumab obtained approval as initial therapy, administered either independently in PD-L1-positive malignancies or together with chemotherapy [9]. Current clinical studies are examining the incorporation of immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in (neo)adjuvant protocols and investigating innovative therapeutic combinations in the recurrent/metastatic context to boost treatment outcomes, extend patient survival and address resistance patterns [10]. Immunotherapy offers new possibilities, surpassing traditional treatments by improving survival rates and reducing toxicity to non-cancerous tissues [11]. However, challenges remain, including drug resistance and the need for more effective methods to assess patient responses. HNSCC tumours evade immune detection by establishing an immunosuppressive microenvironment, which involves the activation and/or proliferation of immune checkpoints like PD-1 and cytotoxic T lymphocyte antigen 4 (CTLA-4), the upregulation of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and alterations in human leukocyte antigen (HLA) class I presentation pathways, which impair tumour antigen processing machinery [12]. These factors foster an environment conducive to tumour evasion and drug resistance. Additionally, high levels of Tregs, tumour-associated macrophages and myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) contribute to inhibitory immune responses [13]. Developing reliable methods to predict patient response to immunotherapy is critical for effective patient selection and cost-efficiency analysis. Therefore, employing advanced technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI), to predict patient responses, identify biomarkers and explore targets to overcome drug resistance and improve prognosis is essential for the successful implementation of immunotherapy in HNSCC.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:

【Conclusion · S0008-p2】However, the future of AI in HNSCC immunotherapy will depend on more than just technological progress. Several critical questions remain that must be addressed to ensure the effective integration of AI into HNSCC immunotherapy. These issues must be collaboratively assessed by ethicists, clinicians, development teams and information technology specialists, as they serve a pivotal function in the development and application of AI models in this domain. Objective analysis of the predictive ability regarding patients’ responses and sensitivity to immunotherapy is crucial, alongside evaluating the impact of AI on clinically relevant metrics and outcomes throughout the course of immunotherapy. Additional investigation is needed to confirm the broad applicability of AI models using larger patient cohorts from multi-institutional studies. Evaluating AI’s applicability across diverse patient populations and clinical settings is also essential. Additionally, the cost-effectiveness of deploying AI solutions must be rigorously examined, particularly given the high costs associated with new, cutting-edge technologies. While AI is expected to improve clinical outcomes and reduce unnecessary immunotherapy use, its most significant impact may be in optimizing resource allocation and enhancing cost-effectiveness. Achieving these benefits will require adjustments in clinical workflows, improved access to technology and potential structural changes. Furthermore, there is a pressing need for clear, standardized processes for the clinical integration of AI, covering everything from technical standards to staff training.

【Conclusion · S0008-p1】The application of AI in HNSCC immunotherapy is rapidly advancing, encompassing both algorithmic innovations and novel clinical use cases. In the coming years, a continuous increase in AI regulatory approvals and clinical trial outcomes will emerge, with applications extending beyond the current typical use of AI as a supportive tool for classification and prediction. Additionally, the emergence of large language models and multimodal data-driven applications is anticipated to further expand AI’s role in this field.

【Application of AI in HNSCC immunotherapy · S0003-p2】Beyond diagnosis, classification and prognosis, AI also serves a pivotal function in HNSCC treatment. Given the complexity of immunotherapy, AI can help manage and interpret these sophisticated treatments, offering tailored therapies to individual patients in the pursuit of personalized medicine [76]. ICB therapy has evolved as an encouraging approach for treating R/M HNSCC. These inhibitors interact with signalling proteins present in immune and neoplastic cells to combat immune escape mechanisms and boost tumour elimination [78]. Although these agents have demonstrated enhanced survival outcomes in HNSCC patients compared to conventional therapies, the majority of individuals show minimal therapeutic response and may experience treatment-induced side effects, along with possible economic burden [12]. Notwithstanding their effectiveness, determining which patients will respond favourably to checkpoint blockade therapy continues to pose a major obstacle. Existing predictive indicators, encompassing tumour mutational burden (TMB) and PD-L1 immunostaining, demonstrate restricted prognostic value [79] (Figure 4).
